clue.text: Support the team that's bottom

blocks.note: to back someone is to support them
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A fan urges loyalty to a club languishing at the foot of the league table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottom' reads as the team's league position, but it is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal names for the buttocks, the part of the body a person sits on.

clue.text: New "Sun" due to come out

indicators.note: letters that come out of their places are free to be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fresh edition of the Sun newspaper is about to hit the newsstands.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper; here it is only three letters to mix with 'due'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unused is fresh and untouched, still in mint condition, which is one meaning of new.

clue.text: Speaking of spreading the bread, but not the first

indicators.note: excluding the first means the opening letter of the phrase's word is dropped

blocks.note: spreading butter on bread is buttering it

explanation.surface: Someone talks about how to put butter on toast, though not the first slice.
explanation.walkthrough: BUTTERING loses its B to leave UTTERING.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter is to say something out loud, so uttering is a synonym for the act of talking.

clue.text: Strange side to the Spanish lorry driver

indicators.note: something strange is out of its usual form, so these letters get rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
el is Spanish for 'the'

explanation.surface: An odd aspect of the Spaniard who drives a heavy goods vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lorry driver' suggests a trucker, but it means what powers the lorry; lorry is British for truck.
explanation.definitionFit: Diesel is the fuel that powers most heavy trucks, so it is literally what drives the vehicle.

clue.text: By taking a shower, becomes clever?

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a shower is a spell of rain

explanation.surface: A whimsical question: does standing in a shower make one smarter?
explanation.definitionFit: Someone brainy has plenty of brains, meaning they are intelligent and quick-witted.

clue.text: Song about everything sinful

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word wraps around the other

blocks.note: all means everything
bad means wicked or sinful

explanation.surface: A song whose subject is every kind of wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballad is a narrative song or a slow sentimental popular song.

clue.text: Street on the Circle Line

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for Street
a ring is a circle

explanation.surface: A London street that lies on the Circle Line of the Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground route; here 'Circle' and 'Line' are split apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A string is a thin cord, and a line is likewise a length of cord or thread.

clue.text: Money which snooker players pocket?

blocks.note: first meaning: slang for cash, from the colour of dollar bills
second meaning: the green-coloured balls potted in snooker

explanation.surface: Players pocketing prize money at a snooker tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: Snooker is a cue sport like pool; one ball is green, and 'pocket' means pot as well as take money.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang calls banknotes this because dollars are green, and snooker tables carry a coloured ball named after that colour.

clue.text: Churchgoers raised argument with those sending goods abroad

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word makes it read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a row is a quarrel, rhyming with 'cow'
shippers send goods by sea or air

explanation.surface: Members of a congregation pick a fight with some exporters.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who attend church services worship there, so a congregation is made of these people.

clue.text: Extinguishes some fires; lake supplies the water

indicators.note: some of the following words means only a run of their letters is wanted

blocks.note: found spanning the end of fires, all of lake and the start of supplies
surface padding that completes the firefighting picture

explanation.surface: Firefighters put out blazes using water drawn from a nearby lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The semicolon hides the join; 'the water' finishes the picture, since this word is used of quenching thirst or fire with water.
explanation.definitionFit: To slake is to quench or put out, used of thirst and also of fire or burning lime.

clue.text: Supervisor is above prophet

blocks.note: over means above
a seer foresees the future

explanation.surface: A manager ranks higher than a soothsayer.
explanation.definitionFit: An overseer watches over workers and their tasks, which is what a supervisor does.

clue.text: Duty on one vehicle

blocks.note: a duty is a tax on goods
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A levy charged on a single car.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxi is a hired car with a driver, a kind of motor vehicle.

clue.text: Punish follower for going round home

indicators.note: going round something means encircling it, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: a disciple is a follower of a teacher
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A cult member is chastised for making house calls.
explanation.definitionFit: To discipline someone is to correct or penalise them for wrongdoing, a verb sense matching punish.

clue.text: Music makers who need to know the ropes

definitions.text: Music makers who need to know the ropes

blocks.clueFragment: Music makers who need to know the ropes
blocks.note: surface reading: musicians who must learn the basics of their trade
setter's reading: church tower musicians literally handle ropes to sound their peals

explanation.surface: Musicians who must master the basics of their craft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Know the ropes' is an idiom for being experienced, but these players really do pull ropes to ring church bells.
explanation.definitionFit: Change ringers make music by pulling ropes attached to church bells in a tower.

clue.text: Which makes a speaker more colourful

definitions.text: Which makes a speaker more colourful

blocks.clueFragment: Which makes a speaker more colourful
blocks.note: surface reading: something that livens up an orator's language
setter's reading: the speaker is the mouth, made brighter with cosmetic colour

explanation.surface: Something that makes a public speaker's talk more vivid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colourful' suggests lively language, but it is literal: the cosmetic adds colour to the mouth that speaks.
explanation.definitionFit: This cosmetic is applied to the mouth to tint it red or pink.

clue.text: Helping Capone is sensible!

blocks.note: a ration is a helping or portion
Al Capone was the Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: Assisting the gangster Al Capone is presented as a wise choice.
explanation.definitionFit: Rational means based on reason and logic, so a sensible person acts this way.

clue.text: Sends off for regulations

blocks.note: first meaning: requests goods to be supplied
second meaning: rules or commands

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sends off' hints at a referee dismissing players for rule-breaking, but it is placing a request by post.
explanation.definitionFit: To place a request for goods is a verb sense, while commands or rules issued by authority is the noun sense.

clue.text: Swear there's duck in this part of the meal

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside another

blocks.note: to curse is to swear
a duck is a score of zero in cricket, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A diner swears on finding duck in this stage of dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck in cricket is a batter's score of nothing, so it gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: A course is one stage of a meal, such as a starter, main or dessert.

clue.text: Dip pears in mixture from water-carriers

indicators.note: a mixture is things stirred together, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: dunk pears into a blend made by water-bearers.
explanation.definitionFit: These pipes carry rainwater from roofs and gutters down to the drains.

clue.text: Some of those inside also have standards

indicators.note: some of the following words means only a portion of their letters is used

blocks.note: found across the end of inside and start of also

explanation.surface: Prisoners too can hold moral principles.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideals are principles or values one aims to live by, which is what moral standards are.

clue.text: Fired for cooking cakes and last of bread

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are mixed up
last of means only the final letter of the following word is used

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of bread

explanation.surface: A baker loses their job over the cakes and bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fired' looks like baking in an oven, but it means dismissed from work.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sacked is informal for being dismissed from a job, the same as being fired.

clue.text: Walked round ring road after the first time

indicators.note: round means encircling, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
Rd is the abbreviation for road
a ring is O-shaped

explanation.surface: Someone strolled around a ring road for the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring road' looks like one thing, but road goes round ring, and all of that follows time, which comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Trod is the past tense of tread, meaning stepped or walked.

clue.text: Rat which destroyed red trees

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken apart, so its letters are rebuilt in another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rodent gnaws through some red-leaved trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rat' looks like the animal but is the slang for a turncoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat is slang for a traitor who abandons their side, just as a soldier who flees duty does.

clue.text: Rich, so turns to groups of singers

indicators.note: turns here means changes shape, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wealthy person therefore takes up choral singing.
explanation.definitionFit: Choirs are organised ensembles of vocalists, often performing in churches or concert halls.

clue.text: So US city church offers consolation

blocks.note: taken as written
LA is Los Angeles
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An American city's church provides comfort to the troubled.
explanation.definitionFit: Solace is comfort given to someone in grief or distress, the same as consolation.

clue.text: Threaten people with an expert

blocks.note: men are people
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: Intimidating a crowd by bringing along a specialist.
explanation.definitionFit: To menace someone is to intimidate them with possible harm, a verb meaning threaten.
